fact_keys: domestic demand contracted 3.0% in june 2026, with the steepest falls in china (-5.2%) and japan (-3.8%); brazil domestic traffic was up 0.9% and australia was flat.
iata director general willie walsh attributed the decline largely to domestic market declines in china, the us, and japan, and weak but improving international demand for middle east carriers.
iata reported global air cargo demand (ctk) increased 8.5% year-on-year in june 2026, with capacity (actk) up 4.4%; north american carriers saw the strongest growth at 13.1%.
iata reported total air passenger demand (rpk) was down 1.7% in june 2026 compared to june 2025, with capacity (ask) down 1.3% and load factor at 84.2%.
middle eastern carriers saw a 14% year-on-year decrease in demand in june 2026, with capacity down 11% and load factor at 76.3%; the rate of decline halved month-to-month since april.

willie walsh said air cargo demand growth outpaced global trade, supported by high-value technology products and urgent shipments, with risks from continuing middle east hostilities and renewed us tariff focus.
